headline: Courier van attacked and set on fire in Rayerbazar
summary: A covered van of AJR Courier Service was targeted by attackers on motorcycles, leaving the driver injured and critical documents destroyed.
details: A courier service covered van was attacked and set on fire in front of the agricultural market in Rayerbazar, Dhaka. The driver was injured in the incident, and the company reported that parcels and important documents were destroyed.
Witnesses and employees of AJR Courier Service stated that a group of individuals on 10 to 12 motorcycles intercepted the vehicle while it was heading toward Hazaribagh via the Beribadh road.

The attackers first vandalized the van and then threw petrol bombs, causing the vehicle to catch fire. The company's Assistant General Manager, Jayanta Chowdhury, noted that the van contained critical bank and insurance documents as well as customer parcels.

The courier company claims they are being systematically targeted. They reported a previous attack on October 20 in Hazaribagh, where their office was looted of laptops and goods worth 3.1 million BDT, and CCTV footage was stolen.

The company further alleges that the attackers identified themselves as associates of a local gang leader, Sanjidul Islam Emon, and demanded rent for the land. They also reported an attempted arson attack on their Hazaribagh warehouse on October 25.

Other attacks occurred on October 31, where three vehicles were vandalized and set on fire in Rayerbagh, Motsya Bhaban, and near the Mayor Hanif Flyover toll plaza. One driver was seriously injured in the Motsya Bhaban incident.

Most recently, on Tuesday night, two cocktails were exploded in front of the AJR Pallabi office in Mirpur-11, injuring another employee. Police from the Mohammadpur station are currently working to identify the suspects.

headline_marked: Two DGFI members [[dismissed and jailed for a year]] in extortion case
headline: Two DGFI members dismissed and jailed for a year in extortion case
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were sacked after a court martial found them guilty of attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.
The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested on October 25 after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.
The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.
Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to buy a motorcycle, but was instead confined, assaulted and forced to hand over Tk 70,000.
The businessman escaped the situation by spotting a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli around 3:00 am on October 25.
Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the car they were using.
Following their arrest, the two DGFI members were handed over to the army and tried under military law, leading to their dismissal and sentencing.
caption:
Two DGFI members have been sacked and sentenced to one year in prison for attempting to extort Tk 10 lakh from a businessman.

Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.

The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested on October 25 after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a motorcycle trader in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.

The victim, Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.

Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to buy a motorcycle, but was instead confined, assaulted and forced to hand over Tk 70,000.

The businessman escaped the situation by spotting a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli around 3:00 am on October 25.

Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the car they were using.

Following their arrest, the two DGFI members were handed over to the army and tried under military law, leading to their dismissal and sentencing.
